title: ACT ON SPECIAL DISPOSITION OF VETERANS ASSISTANCE PROPERTY
full_text:
ACT ON SPECIAL DISPOSITION OF VETERANS ASSISTANCE PROPERTY

Article 1 (Purpose)

The purpose of this Act is to enable persons eligible for veterans assistance to develop their capacity for self-support through mutual assistance and, further, to stabilize their livelihoods, by donating State property or vested property that the State has permitted such persons to use or derive profits from to the persons granted that permission. <Amended on Dec. 24, 1974>

Article 2 (Definitions)

(1) The term “persons eligible for veterans assistance” in this Act means persons who fall under any of the following subparagraphs: <Amended on Dec. 24, 1974>

1. Persons who fall under either subparagraph 2 or 3 of Article 2 (1) of the Military Assistance Compensation Act;
2. Wives, children, or parents of deceased wounded military personnel or police officers;
3. Persons who fall under any subparagraph of Article 2 (1) of the Special Assistance Act for Persons of Distinguished Service to the State, etc.;
4. Corporations composed of persons falling under subparagraphs 1 through 3.

(2) The term “veterans assistance property” in this Act means property listed in the attached Table, among all immovable and movable property constituting State property or vested property that the State has permitted persons eligible for veterans assistance to use or derive profits from for the purpose of such assistance.

Article 3 (Donation of Veterans Assistance Property)

(1) Notwithstanding the State Property Act, the Vested Property Disposal Act, the Budget and Accounts Act, and other relevant statutes and regulations, the Administrator of Veterans Affairs may donate veterans assistance property to persons eligible for veterans assistance as prescribed by this Act.

(2) Veterans assistance property that two or more persons have been permitted to use or derive profits from may be donated to those persons in co-ownership.

Article 4 (Repayment of Debts Relating to Veterans Assistance Property)

(1) Where veterans assistance property is subject to an obligation to repay a debt as a result of the establishment of a security interest or otherwise, the person who receives that property as a donation under this Act shall repay the debt.

(2) Veterans assistance property under paragraph (1) shall not be donated until the debt has been repaid. <Amended on Dec. 24, 1974>

Article 5 (Donation Procedures)

Procedures for the donation of veterans assistance property under Article 3 shall be separately prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Dec. 24, 1974>

Article 6 (Prohibition on Sale, Etc.)
Notwithstanding the provisions of the Civil Act and the Civil Procedure Act, veterans assistance property donated under Article 3 shall not be sold, transferred, provided as security, or seized for 5 years from the date of donation (except in cases of disposition for arrears under the National Tax Collection Act): Provided, That an exception shall be made where the approval of the Administrator of Veterans Affairs has been obtained.

Article 7 (Entry of Prohibition on Disposal in the Register)
(1) Where a donee of veterans assistance property applies for registration of ownership of that property, the donee shall attach a deed of donation of veterans assistance property issued by the Administrator of Veterans Affairs.
(2) Upon receipt of an application for registration under paragraph (1), the registration official shall enter in the register the fact that the property is subject to this Act and the prohibitions under Article 6. <Amended on December 24, 1974>

Article 8 (Remission of Overdue Lease Charges, Etc.)
Where lease charges or rent for donated veterans assistance property are in arrears, those arrears shall be remitted simultaneously with the donation of the property concerned.

Article 9 (Exemption from Taxes, Etc.)
The donation of veterans assistance property shall be exempt from income tax, acquisition tax, registration tax, and all other public charges required for registration.

Article 10 (Enforcement Decree)
Matters necessary for the enforcement of this Act shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on December 24, 1974>

ADDENDA <Act No. 1368, July 26, 1963>
This Act shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.
